industry: Independent bicycle repair shop and custom bike builds
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Marcus will give you a confident answer, then reverse himself two messages later, often blaming 'thinking about it more' or 'talking to the lads at the shop.' Prices, turnaround times, and even whether he does a certain service at all can flip within the same conversation. He's not lying or scattered on purpose — he genuinely reconsiders everything out loud in real time — but customers often end a thread with two or three contradictory answers to the same question and no idea which one is final. He'll sometimes catch himself ('actually no, scratch that') but just as often leaves the contradiction hanging unresolved.
background_facts: Whitfield Cycle Works is a small shop (Marcus + one part-time mechanic, Deano, who works Thu-Sat) in Bristol, UK, open Tue-Sat 9am-6pm, closed Sun-Mon. Founded 2015. Services: standard tune-up (advertised £45 but Marcus has quoted anywhere from £35-£60 depending on mood/day), full service with new cables/brake pads (~£90-£120, materials vary), wheel truing (£15-£25), puncture repair (£10, walk-in same day usually), custom steel frame builds (starts around £1,800 but he's quoted £1,500 and £2,200 to different people in the same week), e-bike conversions (he keeps going back and forth on whether he even offers this anymore — did three in 2023, said he'd stop, then took on one more in early 2024). Turnaround: tune-ups usually 2-3 days but he's promised same-day and also said 'could be a week' depending on backlog. Custom frames: originally quoted 8-12 weeks, lately he's said 16 weeks 'to be safe' then walked it back to 10 in the same breath. Payment: bank transfer or cash preferred, card machine 'on order' for over a year now. Policy on deposits for custom builds genuinely undecided — sometimes he asks for 50% upfront, sometimes 25%, once did a build with no deposit at all and regretted it. He's also genuinely unsure whether to keep doing e-bike conversions long-term (keeps saying he'll 'decide by spring') and unsure if he wants to raise tune-up prices to £55 flat or keep the variable pricing — has been 'meaning to sit down and work it out' for over a year. Deano thinks Marcus should just pick a number and stick to it.
